children: Wall Street ended lower but did pare some losses Thursday as investors weighed discussions over reopening the Strait of Hormuz and economic fallout from the Iran war.
Seeking Alpha analyst Leo Nelissen of
said the session was “entirely about the Iran War,” arguing that markets are at a critical point as the conflict disrupts energy supplies.

“The longer the conflict takes, the higher the inflation risks,” Nelissen stated, pointing to global energy supplies at multi-year lows. He said those pressures have altered monetary policy expectations.
Before the war, markets were pricing in three Federal Reserve rate cuts, but Nelissen said investors now anticipate four hikes, including the latest 25-basis-point hike.
Nelissen also highlighted rising Treasury yields as a growing threat to economic activity. “With 10-year rates breaking out, the pressure on the ‘real economy’ is now elevated,” he said.
For now, he added, investors remain dependent on the AI trade to support markets in the near term through this period.

title: SA analyst warns Iran war is driving inflation risks higher
